content: Dr. André Briend has a wealth of experience in the fields of research, program management, and pediatrics. He was a member of the technical staff in the Department of Child and Adolescent Health and Development at the World Health Organization (WHO) until 2010. Currently, he works as an independent consultant. Dr. Briend played a pivotal role in the development of the patent for the ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) known as Plumpy’Nut. However, he does not own the rights to this product and does not receive any royalties from it. The patent for Plumpy’Nut is held by Nutriset and the Institut de Recherche pour le Développement. It was agreed that this information would be disclosed in the relevant guidelines. Dr. Mark Manary is a Professor of Pediatrics at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, USA. He also serves as the director of the Global Harvest Alliance, a collaborative initiative between the St. Louis Children’s Hospital and the Donald Danforth Plant Science Center. His research primarily focuses on various aspects of nutrition in populations from developing countries, with a particular emphasis on Malawi, Africa. Over the past three years, Dr. Manary has been active in academia and is the founder of the non-governmental organization (NGO) Project Peanut Butter. This organization produces ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) for use in nutrition programs in Malawi and Sierra Leone. Project Peanut Butter operates as a charitable initiative, selling RUTF on a cost-recovery basis to governments and agencies, which then distribute it free of charge to malnourished children. It was determined that Dr. Manary’s humanitarian work with Project Peanut Butter would also be reported in the guidelines. The recommendations outlined in this global guideline are scheduled for review in 2020. If new information becomes available at that time, a guideline review group will be convened to assess the evidence and revise the recommendations accordingly. The Department of Nutrition for Health and Development at WHO headquarters in Geneva, in collaboration with its internal partners, will oversee the coordination of the guideline update, adhering to the formal procedures outlined in the WHO handbook for guideline development. WHO also welcomes suggestions for additional questions to be evaluated during the guideline review process.
